title.narrative: FOOD SECURITY THROUGH CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND GENDER EQUALITY

description.narrative: The ‘Food Security through Climate Resilience and Gender Equality’ project aims to reduce hunger and malnutrition and promote gender equality among smallholder farmers in the districts of Teso, in North East Uganda. The implementing partners are Kaberamaido Operation Save the Needy, Katakwi Conserve Uganda, Katakwi Integrated Development Organisation, Akura Kuo Women’s Group, and Aipectoi Apoloros Farmers’ Group. The objective is to support smallholder farmers to increase their skills and knowledge to benefit nutritionally and economically from a diversified production while also increasing their skills to conduct business operations effectively. Farmers will also be supported to adopt climate resilient approaches to food production as well as building their capacity to advocate for their rights including gender equality and the right to food. The key activities include mobilising local government structures to organise the targeted smallholder farmers into farmers groups; training to build their capacities in group dynamics, Good Agronomic Practices, livestock management, post-harvest handling, kitchen gardening, and nutrition-sensitive agriculture; creating Village Savings and Loans Associations services; training in business skills, linkages with banks and microfinance institutions, and linkages with private sector actors; and trainings on gender and disability mainstreaming, advocacy and lobbying, safeguarding, and engagement of local government extension services.
